method.candidate_universe: Every Wave 01 record classified candidate_requires_field_audit; controls and requires-additional-acquisition rows remain in their original classes.
method.chain_rule: provisional_ccd_chain_depth is the deepest uninterrupted documented stage beginning at stage 0; it is null when stage 0 is not documented.
method.furthest_rule: furthest_documented_stage records the most downstream documented fact without bridging any earlier causal gap.
method.promotion_rule: A supported_for_human_review disposition means the official packet warrants independent event adjudication; it does not create an included K0 event or publication clearance.

rows.matter: FAA flight-safety inspector qualification disclosure and retaliation
rows.institution: Federal Aviation Administration / Office of Special Counsel
rows.qualification_basis: Aviation Safety Inspector responsible for safety oversight.

source_packets.supports: FAA's April 2019 statement that all relevant inspectors were fully qualified; an agency audit found major formal-training and certification deficiencies.
Underlying safety concern and retaliation were substantiated; duties and training opportunities were removed or denied and the matter settled.

stage_assessments.basis: FAA told a Senate committee that all relevant inspectors were fully qualified.
A qualified inspector disclosed missing training and certifications; FAA audit findings substantiated the concern.
Retaliatory personnel treatment was substantiated, but the public packet does not record an explicit competence or attitude label applied to the whistleblower.
The packet does not state the managerial explanation before and after the contradiction.
Managers removed duties and denied training, certifications, or opportunities.
The inspector changed positions and cities and later received compensatory damages.
Duties and access were reduced, but the packet does not establish complete removal from the relevant safety-feedback channel.
Redress required external oversight and settlement; the full internal appeal and stay chronology is not in the packet.

open_requirements: managerial explanation before and after the disclosure
whether the whistleblower retained an operative safety-review channel

rows.matter: BARDA safety and efficacy disclosures followed by reassignment
rows.institution: HHS / BARDA / NIH / Office of Special Counsel
rows.qualification_basis: Director of the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority.

source_packets.supports: Safety, efficacy, pandemic-response, and influence concerns; reassignment to a nonsupervisory NIH role; retaliation complaint and settlement.

stage_assessments.basis: The settlement notice does not state the exact HHS proposition being evaluated before the disclosures.
Bright made source-explicit safety, efficacy, and pandemic-response disclosures from the BARDA director role.
The public notice does not identify a competence, loyalty, attitude, or capture classification applied by HHS.
The official rationale for reassignment before and after the disclosures is not supplied.
HHS reassigned Bright to a nonsupervisory NIH role.
The reassignment limited his role in the pandemic response.
The dissenting program leader was removed from BARDA supervisory authority.
OSC investigated and facilitated settlement, but the notice does not adjudicate retaliation or provide the complete pre-action stay and remedy chronology.

open_requirements: exact governing proposition and decision record
merits disposition or complete settlement instrument

rows.matter: CBP helicopter-safety disclosure, report editing, and hostile working conditions
rows.institution: Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations / Office of Special Counsel
rows.qualification_basis: Air and Marine Operations safety director.

source_packets.supports: Credible retaliation evidence; executive disparagement and hostility; substantiated removal of crash-report information as a litigation hazard; independent review and policy revision.

stage_assessments.basis: An executive treated critical mishap-report information as a litigation hazard that should be removed.
The safety director disclosed fleet and crash-investigation safety concerns and challenged removal of critical information.
OSC found disparagement and hostility toward the whistleblower and his disclosures, but the public packet does not quote a bounded competence reclassification.
Safety evidence was reframed as legal and reputational exposure—a litigation hazard—to justify removal from the official report.
The executive directed removal of critical information from an Aircraft Mishap Report; management also allowed a hostile work environment.
The official safety record was narrowed and working conditions materially changed; the whistleblower later received compensatory damages.
The hostile environment chilled the safety function, but the packet does not establish the exact causal route from retaliation to retirement or complete loss of the feedback channel.
Correction required OSC referral, Coast Guard review, settlement, and policy revision; the duration and every internal correction route are not fully stated.

open_requirements: exact language and date of the executive's disparagement
complete Aircraft Mishap Report versions and custody history
causal record for retirement and the duration of blocked correction

rows.matter: Army biosafety-laboratory warnings followed by investigation, reassignment, privilege suspension, and proposed removal
rows.institution: U.S. Army / Office of Special Counsel / Merit Systems Protection Board
rows.qualification_basis: Former medical director and Biological Personnel Reliability Program director responsible for medical fitness in secure biosafety laboratories.

source_packets.supports: Qualification, safety disclosures, retaliatory investigation, reassignment, clinical-privilege suspension, proposed firing, idling, OSC retaliation finding, and Army failure to correct.
Eight-year retaliation chronology, MSPB default judgment, settlement, record clearing, reassignment, compensation, and Army admission of no wrongdoing.

stage_assessments.basis: The packets do not identify the exact Army claim about inspection adequacy that the physician was formally asked to evaluate.
A specifically qualified physician reported deficient inspections and discouragement of mishap reporting.
A retaliatory investigation and sharp change from excellent performance treatment are documented, but the competence or loyalty classification itself is not quoted.
The public packets do not provide the Army's substantive rationale for the investigation, reassignment, privilege suspension, or proposed removal.
The Army investigated, reassigned, suspended clinical privileges, proposed removal, and left the physician with little or no work.
Leadership and physician duties, privileges, compensation, reputation, and work were materially affected for years.
The physician was removed from leadership and clinical duties and idled away from the biosafety function.
The Army declined OSC's recommended correction; relief required an OSC complaint, MSPB default judgment, mediation, and settlement after more than eight years.

open_requirements: complete OSC report and MSPB record

rows.matter: Secret Service disclosures followed by security-clearance and employment consequences
rows.institution: United States Secret Service / Department of Homeland Security OIG
rows.qualification_basis: Senior Special Agent with twenty years of investigative and protective duties.

source_packets.supports: Protected disclosures; security-clearance suspension and revocation; administrative leave and indefinite unpaid suspension; first DHS PPD-19 substantiation of retaliatory clearance action.

stage_assessments.basis: The summary does not state the exact Secret Service proposition contradicted by the agent's disclosures.
The senior agent disclosed alleged legal violations and abuse of authority through protected channels.
Retaliatory clearance action was substantiated, but the summary does not identify a competence, trustworthiness, or loyalty label used to justify it.
The clearance rationale before and after the disclosures is absent from the public summary.
The Secret Service suspended and revoked the security clearance and placed the agent on leave and indefinite unpaid suspension.
The agent lost clearance, duties, pay, and operative professional standing.
Clearance revocation and suspension removed the agent from investigative and protective work.
The summary does not state the final corrective action, restoration, or duration of blocked review.

open_requirements: clearance decision instruments and stated rationale
